knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")

## Overview

`lifewatt` reports environmental justice indicators at the granularity each
source actually publishes:

- **by state** — residential electricity price (observed EIA-861 annual and EIA
  B1 monthly series) with YoY / MoM trends, bill-as-evidence price views, and an
  expected life-expectancy loss view anchored to published national life tables
  (NCHS), where any life-expectancy translation is a caller-supplied sensitivity
  parameter;
- **by state** — a synthetic life-expectancy estimate (state mortality rates +
  national life-table anchor; every assumption declared in
  `sensitivity_assumption`);
- **by ZCTA** — CDC PLACES adult health prevalence for the ZCTA that matches a
  ZIP code.

No source publishes a realised average residential price per ZIP code, so the
price layer takes a state and refuses a ZIP by name.

## Workflow

```{r eval = FALSE}
library(lifewatt)

# observed annual price, state-level (customer-weighted across the state's utilities)
electricity_price("FL", year = 2024)

# state monthly series (2023-01 .. 2026-07; EIA-preliminary months flagged)
electricity_price("FL", period = "mom")

# trends
electricity_price_trend("FL", period = "yoy")
electricity_price_trend("FL", period = "mom")

# price + bill evidence (bill is Bayesian evidence, not a required input)
my_electricity("FL", bill = 180, time = "2026-12")
my_electricity("FL", bill = 180, usage = 1200, time = "2026-12")

# expected life-expectancy loss view
expected_life_loss("FL", "2026-07")
expected_life_loss("FL", "2026-12", bill = 180, usage = 1200)
expected_life_loss("FL", "2026-09", delta_le = 0.01)

# adult health estimates for the ZCTA (CDC PLACES 2025 release, BRFSS 2023;
# downloaded live from data.cdc.gov on each call)
health_measure("32601")
health_measure("32601", measure = c("DIABETES", "BPHIGH"))
```

Price and life-expectancy functions accept a two-letter USPS code or a full
state name; a ZIP code is refused by name and the error points at the state
form. `health_measure()` is the exception: CDC PLACES publishes by ZCTA, so it
needs a ZIP and says so when handed a state.

## Provenance and honesty contract

Every returned row carries provenance columns (`source`, `level`,
`degraded_from`, `mapping_vintage`, `provisional`). On price and
life-expectancy rows `level` is always `"state"` and `degraded_from` is always
`NA`: nothing is degraded from a ZIP, because the interface no longer accepts
one. `health_measure()` rows are `level = "zcta"` with `degraded_from = "zip"`,
because a ZIP is treated as the ZCTA with the same five digits.

Months EIA still marks Preliminary are flagged provisional; months after 2026-07
are served by the LSTM price forecast (`fit_as_of = 2026-07`).
`health_measure()` is the exception on provenance *epochs* rather than on
columns: it is the only interface that is not served from a shipped snapshot, so
its `provisional` flag is always `FALSE` while the bytes come from a live
query.

The annual row also carries `price_min`, `price_max` and `n_utility` for the
state's utilities, and every state-level row carries `within_state_sd`. Those
three numbers are how the package states, per row, how far the state value can
sit from a particular ZIP.

`delta_le` is a declared sensitivity parameter, not a sourced elasticity: the
output labels it in a `sensitivity_assumption` column. Without `delta_le` the
life-loss columns are withheld. `life_expectancy()` / `life_expectancy_trend()`
return **synthetic** estimates (mortality-based D1b/D2 sensitivity synthesis);
the `estimate_type` label states they are not NCHS-published subnational life
expectancies, and all synthesis assumptions travel in `sensitivity_assumption`.
The mortality source is quarterly (NCHS VSRR provisional), so trend periods are
`"yoy"` / `"qoq"` — `"mom"` is refused honestly.

```{r eval = FALSE}
life_expectancy("FL")
life_expectancy("FL", quarter = "2024Q4")
life_expectancy_trend("FL", period = "yoy")
```
